From: Samantha Liu <samantha.liu@orionhealthsys.com>

Cc: procurement@orionhealthsys.com
Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Request: custom availability rider + evidence requirements

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for the demo last week — Orion is excited about Redwood's predictable latency profile. Procurement asked me to follow up with a formal request: we need an availability rider that ties uptime to the order form for our enterprise MSA/SOW. Key asks:

- 99.95% monthly availability for the hosted inference endpoint used by Orion production clusters.
- A latency safeguard (p95 < 350ms for standard gen requests) with an accompanying credit schedule for sustained breaches.
- A clearly defined evidence list for any credits (uptime reports, raw telemetry slices, SOC 2 extract).
- Documentation of fallback behavior: if Redwood must failover to a reduced tier model, we need transparent routing & metrics.

I've attached a sample appendix the legal team drafted (Orion-SLA-Appendix-v1.pdf). Can Redwood provide a redline of the order form and proposed exhibit language? Also, procurement needs a mapping of evidence we can request during audits.

Appreciate a proposed timeline — procurement is targeting signature by the end of July.

Best,
Samantha Liu
Director, Vendor Management
Orion Health Systems

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the appendix. We're aligned on the overall shape. High level response and next steps:  

1) Availability & latency: Redwood can commit to a 99.95% monthly availability for the named endpoint under the Dedicated capacity arrangement. For hosted multi-tenant customers we'll propose equivalent protections via Dedicated reserved capacity. Latency credit schedule: attached is a proposed table (in the redline doc) that scales credits if p95 breaches exceed agreed thresholds over a 72-hour window.

2) Evidence & audits: we'll provide token-level uptime reports (per-route), request-level traces for root-cause analysis, and a SOC 2 extracts export (time-bound). For on-prem / private deployments we can also provide host-level telemetry. I'll include an evidence matrix mapping each credit condition to the artifact type.

3) Fallback & model-tiering: we can define a routing policy that favors model variant pinning and only falls back to compatible model variants with explicit notification windows. We'll include runbook excerpts in the exhibit for transparency.

4) Timeline: I can share a redline by EOD tomorrow, then propose a 72-hour internal review and a call with your procurement/legal next week. If that works, we'll circulate DocuSign-ready exhibit + order form.

Attaching: Redwood-orderform-uptime-rider-redline.docx (redline of order form + exhibit), evidence-matrix-soc2-ksm.csv (mapping).

Thanks — Karthik

Subject: Internal: redline notes for Orion appendix

Team — attaching my initial pass on the redline. Highlights:

- I converted the '99.95% monthly' ask into two variants: (A) Dedicated Reservation: 99.95% monthly availability guaranteed in the order form; (B) Hosted + Reserved Add-on: operational target 99.95% (no SLA) + enhanced monitoring + service credits limited to burst protection. Legal will push for option A.
- Credit calc: propose rolling 30-day window for measuring availability, with a backstop of calendar-month reconciliation for billing credits. That gives us operational flexibility while giving them the predictable credit outcome they want.
- Evidence: we can provide per-route request logs, per-token cost slices, and 30-day SOC 2 export. Anything more than that requires custom ingestion agreements due to data residency.

I also added a clause that defines "degraded mode" and the automated notification cadence (T+15m post-detect, T+1h update).

Kimberly Park
Sr. Contracts Manager
Redwood Inference
